title: Policy-driven continuous batching thermostat and workload profiler
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a policy-driven continuous batching "thermostat" service that: (1) profiles live workloads to extract temporal and per-route sequence-length, concurrency, and KV cache reuse signals; (2) synthesizes conservative heuristic batching+cache parameter recommendations; (3) performs safe candidate application via simulation, shadow-apply, and canary rollout with automated rollback on defined SLO/cost gates. Goal: reduce per-token cost while keeping P99 latency and error-rate within SLAs.
comments: 2026-01-12 - Ava Chen: Initial RFC submitted. Problem: we currently have ad-hoc batch configs per-customer; ops want automated, safe tuning that can run continuously and roll back without impacting live traffic. Proposed components: profiler, heuristic composer, simulator, rollout manager. Links to RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/continuous-batching-thermostat

2026-01-18 - Diego Martinez: Spike complete. Prototype profiler collects: per-route seq-length histogram, inter-arrival distribution, KV cache hit-rate by prompt prefix, and tail-latency contributions by token index. Using 24h rolling windows and exponential decay. Saved sample outputs in GCS: gs://redwood-inference/thermostat/spike/2026-01-18.tar.gz

2026-01-22 - Priya Kapoor (PM): Reviewed spike. Requested stronger safety: (a) deterministic simulation mode that runs historical traffic through candidate batch policy; (b) explicit rollout gates: delta-cost <= 10% and P99 latency delta <= +5% for 1h canary; otherwise abort and rollback. Added requirement to include manual override and mute-trigger for on-call SREs.

2026-01-25 - Diego Martinez: Implemented simulator that replays sampled requests against a micro-runtime to estimate token throughput and KV-cache warms. Simulator shows median estimated cost reduction of 12% on sample LLM workload A, but tail increases in some routes. Attached PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4789

2026-01-29 - Design review (Maya Singh): UX for Console: show active thermostat recommendations per-route, confidence score, expected cost delta, rollback button, and a timeline of simulation vs live metrics. Wireframes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ThermostatWireframes

2026-02-01 - Diego Martinez: Introduced policy composer. Policies are expressed as prioritized heuristics (e.g., prefer microbatch size 8 for seq<=96, prefer microbatch size 64 for bursty low-latency routes) plus safety knobs (max-p99-regression, max-cost-upside). Implemented transactional apply with pre-checks and a shadow-apply pathway.

2026-02-03 - QA update (Ravi Patel): Started canary tests in staging with 2 customer-simulated workloads. Observed one route with high KV-cache churn causing P99 +8%. Canary aborted and thermostat rolled back automatically. Root cause: cache-eviction policy didn't pin prefixes used by long-running chat sessions. Action: add cache-affinity heuristic and repeat canary.

Next steps: (1) add cache-affinity heuristic and re-run canary on the failing route; (2) add cost-explainability output to Console (breakdown by batching vs caching); (3) integration tests for transactional rollback under flaky infra. Owners: Diego (engine), Priya (PM), Maya (design).
